summary: An excerpt from a fiction narrative in which a young narrator and his companion Ange are kissing near a church pillar in a park when the atmosphere turns violent. Loudspeakers issue orders to disperse as an illegal gathering, riot police in Darth Vader-style helmets advance banging truncheons on shields, and helicopters circle overhead. The crowd, rallied by a band called Trudy Doo, chants "TAKE IT BACK!" and surges toward the police lines, and the narrator, sheltering Ange in a church doorway, reflects that he now knows what war must be like.
one_line: A narrator and Ange are interrupted by a police crackdown on an illegal park gathering, where a band rallies a crowd to "TAKE IT BACK!"
key_facts: The narrator and Ange cross to a church with big pillars in front of it after holding hands and moving quickly.
Ange whispers "It undoes in the back" while the narrator is kissing her.
The narrator fumbles with the hook of Ange's bra and describes himself as bad at undoing it.
The sirens start just as the narrator brushes the sides of Ange's breasts.
A voice repeatedly orders "DISPERSE IMMEDIATELY" and says "THIS IS AN ILLEGAL GATHERING."
The band stopped playing when the orders began, and the crowd across the street became scared and angry.
The PA system is powered by car-speakers and car-batteries in the tennis courts.
The crowd chants "TAKE IT BACK!" in answer to the PA's roar.
Police move in lines carrying plastic shields, wearing Darth Vader helmets, with black truncheons and infra-red goggles.
Police bang their truncheons on their shields with each step forward.
Helicopters are overhead with no floodlights, and the narrator infers they have infrared scopes.
The rebel yell belongs to Trudy Doo, whose guitar, drums and bass play as the PA roars.
The crowd boils out of the park at the police lines.
The narrator says he has never been in a war but now thinks he knows what it must be like.
